activities.anchor: Around 6-7 million years ago our lineage separated
activities.caption: put the split on the deep-time scale
activities.name: anHomininSplitPlace

config.prompt: When did our lineage separate from the ancestors of chimpanzees? Place the marker on the scale.
config.why: Roughly 6–7 million years ago, per the genetic molecular clock. The split was a branching: one population became both lineages, so chimpanzees are cousins, not ancestors.

activities.caption: bet on what came first
activities.name: anLaetoliPredict

config.q: The Laetoli footprints (3.66 mya) show two individuals walking upright. What do they prove about the order of human adaptations?
choices: Big brains evolved first, then upright walking followed
Upright walking came first, with chimp-sized brains doing the thinking
Tools and brains evolved together in a single package
Upright walking and big brains appeared simultaneously
config.why: Bipedality was locked in well before any brain expansion — the defining human adaptation came first, with chimp-sized brains doing the thinking.

activities.anchor: given way to a mosaic-forest picture
activities.caption: find the faulty line in this origin story
activities.name: anSavannahSpot

config.prompt: A student writes up the origins of bipedality. One line is wrong — find it.
lines: The earliest candidates are fragmentary: Sahelanthropus, Orrorin and the better-preserved Ardipithecus.
The surprise of Ardi was ecological: it lived in open savannah, confirming the old savannah hypothesis.
The savannah hypothesis — upright walking evolved to stride across new grasslands — has given way to a mosaic-forest picture.
Bipedality emerged in trees-adjacent habitats, probably for cheaper travel between food patches and better thermoregulation.
Ardi had a grasping, opposable big toe.
config.correction: The surprise of Ardi was that it lived in WOODLAND, not open savannah — which is exactly what undermined the savannah hypothesis.
config.why: The mosaic-forest picture replaced the grassland story: bipedality emerged in trees-adjacent habitats for a bundle of reasons — energetically cheaper travel, carrying, thermoregulation in the open, free hands.

activities.anchor: The middle Pleistocene is not a ladder but a shrub
activities.caption: file each species by its place in the bush
activities.name: anBushBuckets

config.prompt: For most of the last million years several kinds of human were alive at once. File each:

items.label: Neanderthals — cold-adapted, the largest brains in the record
Denisovans — discovered by a genome, matched later by a Tibetan jaw
H. floresiensis — the 1.1 m 'hobbit' of Flores, surviving to ~50 kya

config.why: The middle Pleistocene is not a ladder but a shrub. The 'when did we become human?' question dissolves: different humannesses appeared at different times in different bodies.

activities.anchor: non-African genomes carry about 1-2% Neanderthal DNA
activities.caption: guess the Neanderthal share in your genome
activities.name: anNeanderthalEstimate

config.prompt: Roughly what percentage of a non-African genome comes from Neanderthals?
config.why: About 1–2%, slightly more in East Asians. Melanesians carry about 4–6% Denisovan. Interbreeding was normal — the clean-replacement story is dead.
config.context: A couple of percent — and some of it is functional, like the EPAS1 variant that lets Tibetans thrive at 4,000 metres.

activities.anchor: evolution runs from primitive to advanced
activities.caption: true or false — the ladder myth
activities.name: anLadderJudge

statements.s: Evolution runs from primitive to advanced, ending in us.
statements.why: It runs from ancestors to descendants, branching as it goes, with no direction and no goal.

statements.s: Neanderthals were a failed prototype of humanity.
statements.why: They were a successful cold-adapted sibling species that dominated Europe for 300,000 years.

statements.s: Most human 'primitive' claims have decayed under better data.
statements.why: The Neanderthal file is the model case: discovered in 1856 and misread for a century as shambling brutes, then sequentially redeemed by evidence.

statements.s: Our lineage's uniqueness is an accident of the last few millennia.
statements.why: Not a predetermined summit. Several kinds of human were alive at once for most of the last million years.

activities.caption: pair each clock with its material and range
activities.name: anDatingMatch

config.prompt: The timeline is only as good as its clocks. Match each to what it dates:

pairs.right: volcanic tuffs sandwiching the East African fossils — millions of years
cave flowstone and calcite crusts — the method behind Neanderthal cave-art claims
once-living material, but only back to about 50,000 years
a second independent clock — divergence dates calibrated by the fossil record

config.why: Radiocarbon is useless for a million-year-old Homo erectus whose bones have turned to stone. When fossils, dates and genomes agree the confidence is real; when they disagree, the disagreement is the discovery.

activities.caption: reason from the skeleton
activities.name: anCareBranch

config.root: Shanidar 1: a Neanderthal man who survived to old age blind in one eye, with a withered arm and a healed amputation.

start.text: What does a skeleton with that combination of healed injuries tell you?

choices.label: That he was lucky, and Neanderthal life was brutal
choices.feedback: Luck does not heal a withered arm or keep a blind man fed for decades.

choices.label: That others sustained him — a record of care
choices.feedback: Such infirmities lived with, for decades, are a record of care.

lucky.text: You have read the trauma and missed the biography: the survival itself is the evidence, and it required other people.

care.text: The biological anthropologists' line stands. Alongside eagle-talon jewellery at Krapina and prepared-core technology, care is one of the findings that rehabilitated the species.

config.why: The rehabilitation is not sentimental; it is what the evidence says — and it teaches the general discipline of the field: every 'primitive' claim about ancient humans has so far decayed under better data.

activities.caption: drag between family and household
activities.name: anNayarCompare

config.prompt: Two terms that routinely fail to coincide. Drag the divider.

before.label: family — the kinship reckoning
before.text: Who counts as kin. In a Nayar tharavad this held siblings, sisters' children and mothers' brothers — no nuclear core at all, with children belonging to their mother's lineage.

after.label: household — the co-resident unit
after.text: Who shares a roof and tasks. Nayar men lived in their sisters' matrilineal households, and marriage bonds were visiting arrangements with no shared household or paternity rights worth the name.

config.why: The conjugal family can be reduced to near-irrelevance. The modern Western nuclear family is historically peculiar — Coontz traces it to industrial wages, and its 'naturalness' is a recency illusion.

activities.caption: file the three designs of descent
activities.name: anDescentBuckets

config.prompt: Murdock's sample gives three main designs. File each society:

items.label: membership through mothers, with the mother's brother as the key male figure
both lines — kindred, not lineage, as in the modern West

config.why: Matriliny is not matriarchy: no confirmed society has women systematically holding authority over men, and in matrilineal groups senior men — the mother's brother — usually manage lineage affairs.

activities.anchor: the husband-father wants his children's labour
activities.caption: find the faulty line in this descent argument
activities.name: anMatrilinealSpot

config.prompt: A student explains matriliny. One line is wrong — find it.
lines: Descent decides which set of relatives you belong to for good: membership, inheritance, identity.
Matriliny means membership flows through mothers' lines, so the key male figure is the mother's brother.
Matriliny is matriarchy — in matrilineal groups women systematically hold authority over men.
Audrey Richards named the resulting tension the matrilineal puzzle: the father wants his children's labour while the lineage owns the children.
Matriliny clusters where hoe horticulture gives women a central production role; plough agriculture and herding track patriliny.
config.correction: Matriliny is NOT matriarchy — no confirmed society has women systematically holding authority over men; senior men usually manage lineage affairs.
config.why: The design question is always 'who transfers what to whom', not 'who is boss'. On the transfer question matriliny is as rule-bound as patriliny.

activities.anchor: Residence is the second design variable
activities.caption: pair each residence rule with where the couple lands
activities.name: anResidenceMatch

config.prompt: Residence interacts with descent. Match each rule to its arrangement:

pairs.right: with the husband's family — the majority, and the structural root of the precarious daughter-in-law
with the wife's — women on home ground with brothers nearby, security designed in
a fresh household — the modern Western default
with the mother's brother — a matrilineal specialty

config.why: Residence rules are, in effect, gender-relation policies: patriliny plus patrilocality means a bride moves into a house of strangers with authority over her.

activities.caption: rebuild the segmentary logic
activities.name: anSegmentaryOrder

config.prompt: Evans-Pritchard's Nuer ran politics without a state. Put the logic in order:
items: The lineage is a corporate group that holds land collectively and outlives its members
Disputes are handled within the smallest relevant branch of the lineage
When the dispute crosses into a larger branch, the smaller branches fuse against it
Against a common outside threat, the whole people fuses
config.why: 'Me against my brother; my brother and me against my cousin...' — an ordered anarchy achieving law and defence without a state.

activities.caption: bet on the ecology of marriage
activities.name: anPolyandryPredict

config.q: Why did fraternal polyandry — brothers sharing one wife — persist in marginal high-altitude Tibet?
choices: A religious prohibition on dividing households
Partitioning the family land would ruin every heir, so the land stays whole and so does the household
A shortage of women caused by high male mortality
config.why: Goldstein's classic study: in a marginal economy, partitioning the land would ruin every heir, so the land stays whole and so does the household. Marriage rules are political economy.

activities.caption: guess the scale of the dowry danger
activities.name: anDowryEstimate

config.prompt: Roughly what share of all marriages in much of the Middle East, North Africa and South Asia are first-cousin or closer?
config.why: A fifth to half, so roughly a third is a fair midpoint — consolidating property, keeping daughters near, honouring the alliance, with genetic counselling now the modern counterweight.
config.context: Between one in five and one in two — the alliance logic is durable.

activities.caption: true or false — what the transfer actually moves
activities.name: anBridewealthJudge

statements.s: Bridewealth is a man buying a wife.
statements.why: It transfers rights — chiefly over the children's lineage membership. Refund rules when marriages fail show it was never a purchase of a person.

statements.s: Dowry is premortem inheritance — a daughter's share of family property moving with her.
statements.why: Goody tied the direction to property systems: plough agriculture and deep stratification concentrate property worth endowing a daughter.

statements.s: Bridewealth cattle circulate onward to fund other sons' marriages.
statements.why: A circulating political economy, not a stockpiled fee.
It has become global infrastructure — remittances are kinship obligation denominated in cash.

activities.caption: guess what LiDAR found without a trowel
activities.name: anLidarEstimate

config.prompt: The 2018 PACUNAM LiDAR survey of Guatemala's Petén revealed how many previously unmapped structures?
config.why: Tens of thousands — causeways, terraces and fortifications joining city to city, with Late Classic population estimates revised upward to millions.
config.context: A landscape emptied by conquest and overgrowth turned out to be one of the densest pre-industrial settlement systems known.

activities.anchor: the find's position in the three-dimensional record
activities.caption: pair each principle with what it tells you
activities.name: anContextMatch

config.prompt: Excavation is controlled destruction, and context governs everything. Match each principle to its reasoning:

pairs.right: deeper is older — layers stack in depositional order
a thing cut into is older than the cut; the fill is younger than the wall it abuts
what a find lies with, which is what makes it evidence
the whole sequence formalised into a flowchart a site can share

config.why: An artefact with context is evidence; without it, a trophy. A looted pot can be dated by style, but its layer, household and trade route are unrecoverable.

activities.caption: true or false — the depth ruler
activities.name: anSuperpositionJudge

statements.s: Deeper is always older, without exception.
statements.why: Superposition is the default, but a pit, grave or robber-trench cut down through earlier layers fills with later material.

statements.s: A Roman coin can sit beneath a Neolithic one.
statements.why: Without any miracle — the layers interleaved, and the Harris matrix exists precisely because they do.

statements.s: The unit of evidence is the assemblage, not the beautiful object.
statements.why: The museum case is the by-product. A single gold mask tells less than a thousand recorded potsherds.

statements.s: A looted pot loses its information value entirely.
statements.why: Its style can still be dated, but everything it knew about its context is unrecoverable — which is why the antiquities trade is an information crime.

activities.caption: file each dating clock by its material
activities.name: anClockBuckets

config.prompt: Each clock has a material and a range. File them:

items.label: thermoluminescence and OSL — the last time it saw light or heat
potassium-argon and argon-argon — millions of years
uranium-series — the method behind the Neanderthal cave-art claims

config.why: The rule of practice: multiple clocks on one context, cross-checked. A date supported by two independent methods is a finding; one method alone is a hypothesis.

activities.caption: choose the bridge from static to dynamic
activities.name: anMiddleRangeBranch

config.root: You excavate a scatter of stone flakes and butchered bone. The record is frozen; the past was moving. How do you read it?

start.text: What gets you from the static deposit to the dynamic behaviour?

choices.label: Assume the pattern means what it looks like
choices.feedback: That is how taphonomy surprises people — bones scatter, decay and move.

choices.label: Calibrate against present-day processes that leave deposits
choices.feedback: Knap stone experimentally, watch butchers mark bone, study how bones decay — then read the ancient traces.

assume.text: You have read a garbage dump as a butchery floor, and the interpretation is now unfalsifiable.

calibrate.text: Middle range theory: observe present processes, then read the ancient traces against the calibrated dictionary. Hodder adds the second bridge — meaning — using the same dictionary of plausible meanings.

config.why: And the most honest instrument archaeology has is garbage: Rathje's Tucson Garbage Project found households systematically under-reported alcohol while the bins told the truth. Written sources flatter; middens do not.

activities.anchor: The measurement yields a radiocarbon age
activities.caption: fill what a date actually is
activities.name: anCalibrationCloze

config.text: A radiocarbon measurement yields a radiocarbon age that must be %%0%% against tree-ring records, because atmospheric carbon-14 has fluctuated through time. So reports give calibrated ranges, often a century or two wide, and 'BP' means before %%1%%, not before today.
config.hint: The verb names the tree-ring correction step; the year is the radiocarbon convention's fixed reference point.

activities.caption: reverse the assumed sequence
activities.name: anGobekliOrder

config.prompt: The old assumed sequence ran farm → surplus → monuments. Put the Göbekli Tepe evidence in order as discovered:
items: Monumental T-shaped stone pillars are built in enclosures by hunter-gatherers
Radiocarbon dates place the construction around 9600 BCE
Farming appears in the region a millennium or more later
The causality must therefore run backward — feasts and building labour pulled cultivation into being
config.why: Collective ceremony was not a luxury agriculture paid for. The sequence of civilisation is an empirical claim, and excavation keeps amending it.

activities.caption: bet on the bias in the record
activities.name: anAntikytheraPredict

config.q: The Antikythera mechanism — thirty-plus bronze gears computing eclipse calendars, ~100–150 BCE — was found in a shipwreck. What does it teach about the archaeological record?
choices: Ancient technology was uniformly primitive until the Renaissance
The record is a biased sample whose survivors were chosen by material durability, not by capability
Bronze was the only material ancient engineers could work
Eclipse prediction was the central goal of ancient science
config.why: The survivors were chosen by material durability, not by capability. Ancient technology was not uniformly primitive — and each of these cases is the same lesson.
